title: ur aw ore, ou oy, are eer
overview:
New spellings: ur, aw, ore, ou, oy.
The last group of vowel spellings. Then you have them all.
Two letters. One sound.
Do not sound them out one by one.
functions: Say the sound for each new spelling
Read a word that has one in it
Write a word that has one in it
Know where in a word each one goes
Read the new words out loud
Choose between two spellings of one sound
learningPath: Words: the new spellings and the new words.
Write the words from their sounds.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 18. The last of the vowels.
First, three that you already have.
In Unit 14 you met ir and er.
Bird. Her. One sound, two spellings.
Here is the third. Ur. Turn. Burn.
Ir, ur and er. One sound. Three spellings.
Next. In Unit 14 you met or. Fork.
Here are two more ways to write it.
Aw. Saw. Law. Draw.
Ore. More. Store. Before.
Or, aw and ore. One sound. Three spellings.
Now two pairs.
Ou. House. Out. About.
Listen. That is the cow sound from Unit 14.
Ow in cow. Ou in house. The same.
And oy. Boy. Toy. Joy.
That is oi from Unit 14. Coin. Boy.
Oi in the middle. Oy at the end.
That is a real rule and it holds.
Two more that turn up in the words.
Are, as in care. And eer, as in near.
Near uses ear, which you know from hear.
Now one odd word. Work.
It has or in it. But it does not say or.
Work. It says the er sound.
There is a reason, and it is useful.
After a w, the letters or say er.
Work. Word. World. Worse. Worm.
All of them. Every time.
That is Unit 18. You have all the vowels now.

grammar.title: The new spellings: ur, aw, ore, ou, oy
grammar.explanation:
Every sound here is one you already have.
Not one of them is new.
They are the last spellings for the old sounds.
grammar.rule:
ur    as in turn    t - ur - n     same as ir, er
aw    as in saw     s - aw         same as or
ore   as in more    m - ore        same as or
ou    as in house   h - ou - s     same as ow in cow
oy    as in boy     b - oy         same as oi
grammar.workedExample:
You see ur in a word.
1. Do not read two letters.
2. Read one sound.
3. Say that sound out loud.
4. Now find it in turn.
5. Say the sound again there.
grammar.mistake:
Sounding out both letters gives no word at all.
turn is not t - u - r - n.
It is t - ur - n.
grammar.tip: Two letters. Look once. Say once.
grammar.practice:
Say the sound for each one.
1. ur
2. aw
3. ore
4. ou
5. oy
grammar.answers:
Check yourself out loud.
Did you say ONE sound each time?
Two sounds means you read the letters, not the spelling.

grammar.title: Reading a word that has ur, aw, ore, ou, oy in it
grammar.explanation:
Find the two letters first.
Read them as one sound.
Then read the rest of the word.
grammar.rule:
turn     t - ur - n
saw      s - aw
more     m - ore
house    h - ou - s
boy      b - oy
care     c - are
grammar.workedExample:
You see the word saw.
1. Look for the two letters.
2. Cover them with your finger.
3. Read what is left.
4. Now put the one sound back in.
5. Join it all. saw.
grammar.mistake:
Reading left to right, letter by letter, breaks here.
Look for the pair BEFORE you start.
grammar.practice:
Join the sounds and write the word.
1. t - ur - n
2. s - aw
3. m - ore
4. h - ou - s
5. b - oy
6. c - are
grammar.answers:
1. turn
2. saw
3. more
4. house
5. boy
6. care
Five or six right? You can read these.

grammar.title: Writing a word that has ur, aw, ore, ou, oy in it
grammar.explanation:
Say the word. Break it into sounds.
One of those sounds needs TWO letters.
Count sounds, then write.
grammar.rule:
turn     t - ur - n         3 sounds, 4 letters
saw      s - aw             2 sounds, 3 letters
grammar.workedExample:
You want to write more.
1. Say it out loud.
2. Break it: m - ore.
3. Which sound needs two letters?
4. Write that pair together.
5. Read it back to check.
grammar.mistake:
One letter for each sound is wrong now.
The new sound takes two letters.
grammar.tip: Count sounds. Some need two letters.
grammar.practice:
Write the word you hear.
1. more
2. house
3. boy
4. care
5. near
6. work
grammar.answers:
1. more
2. house
3. boy
4. care
5. near
6. work
Five or six right? Good.

grammar.title: ir, ur and er: one sound, three spellings
grammar.explanation:
Three ways to write one sound.
You cannot hear which a word uses.
Position does not help either. Only reading does.
grammar.rule:
ir    bird, girl, first, shirt
ur    turn, burn, hurt, nurse
er    her, water, under, sister

Say all three. The same middle sound.
grammar.workedExample:
You want to write the sound er.
1. Say the word out loud.
2. The sound gives you nothing.
3. Picture the word written down.
4. Write what you have seen.
5. Check it later against a real one.
grammar.mistake:
Waiting for a rule here keeps you stuck.
There is no rule. There is only having read it.
grammar.tip: One sound. Three spellings. Read to learn which.
grammar.practice:
Which spelling? Write ir, ur or er.
1. b__d
2. t__n
3. h__
4. g__l
5. h__t
6. und__
grammar.answers:
1. bird (ir)
2. turn (ur)
3. her (er)
4. girl (ir)
5. hurt (ur)
6. under (er)
You could not hear any of them. That is the point.

grammar.title: After a w, or says er
grammar.explanation:
This one IS a rule, and it holds every time.
After a w, or does not say or.
It says the er sound instead.
grammar.rule:
work    said werk
word    said werd
world   said werld
worse   said werse
worm    said werm

Every w-or word. No exceptions worth knowing.
grammar.workedExample:
You see the word world.
1. Find the or. It is there.
2. Look at the letter before it.
3. It is a w.
4. So the or says er.
5. w - er - l - d. World.
grammar.mistake:
Reading work as work-with-a-fork sound is the slip.
Check for a w in front before you say or.
grammar.practice:
Say each word out loud. Does or say or, or er?
1. work
2. fork
3. word
4. north
5. world
6. short
grammar.answers:
1. er
2. or
3. er
4. or
5. er
6. or
The er ones all have a w in front. Every time.

readings.passage:

He had more than one bag.
I did not care. I had work.
I had to turn and go.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — The new sounds
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat each sound.
ur
aw
ore
ou
oy
ONE sound each. Not two.
Now say each one three times.
Tap the mic. Say them all.
Check: one sound, or did two slip out?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say one of the new sounds. Say it back.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Read the words
speaking.instructions:
Say each word two ways. Slow, then fast.
1. t - ur - n ... turn
2. s - aw ... saw
3. m - ore ... more
4. h - ou - s ... house
5. b - oy ... boy
6. c - are ... care
Tap the mic. Say all six both ways.
Check: was the new spelling one sound?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say three sounds. Join them and say the word.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Say it, then write it
speaking.instructions:
For each word: say it, break it, write it.
1. more
2. house
3. boy
4. care
5. near
6. work
Tap the mic. Say each word and its sounds.
Check: did you say the sounds before you wrote?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for a word with the new spelling. Break it out loud.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Read the list
speaking.instructions:
Read these out loud, straight down the list.
turn
saw
more
house
boy
care
near
work
Do it twice. The second time, try not to stop.
Tap the mic. Read the list twice.
Check: was the second time easier?
speaking.tutor: Read the list to the tutor. Ask which words were not clear.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Three spellings, one sound
speaking.instructions:
Say each word out loud, one after the other.
bird. turn. her. girl. hurt. under.
They all have the same middle sound.
Tap the mic. Say all six.
Check: could you hear any difference? You should not.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say bird, turn and her.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — w plus or
speaking.instructions:
Say each word. Then say or or er.
work. fork. word. north. world. short.
Look for a w in front of the or.
Tap the mic. Do all six.
Check: did the w words all say er?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say work and fork. Not the same.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Words with the new spelling
writing.prompt:
Say each word. Break it into sounds.
Write two letters for the new sound.
writing.criteria:
Six words.
The new spelling written as a pair.
You read each one back after writing it.
writing.extension: Now write one more word with the same spelling.

writing.title: Writing 2 — Sounds and letters
writing.prompt:
Write each word. Then write two numbers.
How many sounds. How many letters.
writing.criteria:
Six words.
Two numbers beside each one.
The numbers are not the same. That is the point.
writing.extension: Find a word where they ARE the same.

quizzes.q: When you see ur you should ___.
quizzes.why: Read the pair as one, not as two letters.

quizzes.q: Join the sounds: t - ur - n. The word is ___.
quizzes.why: The sounds in order make the word.

quizzes.q: Join the sounds: s - aw. The word is ___.
quizzes.why: Find the pair first, then read the rest.

quizzes.q: To write a word with the new spelling you ___.
options: write two letters for that sound
write one letter for each sound
quizzes.a: write two letters for that sound
quizzes.why: The new sound is one sound and two letters.

quizzes.q: How many sounds are in turn?
quizzes.why: Count what you HEAR. There are more letters than sounds.

options: read the pair as one sound
quizzes.a: read the pair as one sound
quizzes.why: Letter by letter is the slow way here.

quizzes.q: You cannot read a word. What do you do first?
quizzes.why: Find the pair, then read around it.

quizzes.q: Bird, turn and her all have ___.
How do you know a word takes ur?
quizzes.why: The sound cannot tell you. Reading can.

quizzes.q: In the word work, the letters or say ___.
quizzes.why: After a w, or says er. Every time.

quizzes.q: Which word has or saying er?
quizzes.why: It is the one with a w in front.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

This is the whole unit, and it goes against everything Units 2 to 7 taught. Expect a learner to read the letters separately for a while. Do not explain it again; point at the pair and say the one sound, and have them say it back. It is a habit, and habits are built by repetition, not by argument.

teacherNotes.type: Find the pair before reading, not during
teacherNotes.note: Left-to-right letter-by-letter reading breaks on these words, because the learner commits to the first letter's sound before they have seen the second. The move is to scan the word for the pair first. A finger under the pair is enough. It looks like a crutch and it is the skill.

From here to the end of the level there are always more letters than sounds. A learner who counts letters will write a spare letter into every word. Have them say the word and count on their fingers before they write.

teacherNotes.type: oi in the middle, oy at the end — this one really is a rule
teacherNotes.note: Most of Book B ends in read it and you will learn it. This one does not: oi never ends a word and oy almost never sits in the middle. Say it as a rule, because a learner who has heard everything else called unpredictable needs to know when they can actually rely on something.

teacherNotes.type: The w-or rule is small, total and worth the two minutes
teacherNotes.note: Work, word, world, worse, worm, worth, worst. Seven common words, one rule, no exceptions a learner will meet. It also explains a word they have been reading wrongly since Unit 14, which is satisfying rather than discouraging.

teacherNotes.type: Say that the vowels are finished
teacherNotes.note: After this unit there is no vowel spelling left to teach. Unit 19 is two consonant spellings and the two sounds of c and g, and Unit 20 is putting it together. A learner who knows the hard part is over reads differently.

assignment.title: Read and write the new words
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Say the sound for each new spelling.
Then read these words, slowly and then faster:
turn, saw, more, house, boy, care
2. Write six of the words from their sounds.
Beside each one, write how many sounds it has.
Listen back before you finish.
